fix_instructions: C1 (ENCODING MISMATCH, all 4 rollouts): Every settlement produces approval_status as "conditionally approved" or "conditionally_approved," yet C1 fails every time. The check's expected string or matching pattern for approval_status does not match how the model naturally encodes a conditional approval. Fix C1's threshold or string matching to accept "conditionally approved," "conditionally_approved," and similar variants containing "conditional." C9 (ENCODING MISMATCH, all 4 rollouts): PF1's "why" references "a conflict-clearance commitment," but no settlement produces a commitment explicitly typed or worded as "conflict clearance" — settlements produce types like "condition_precedent," "ethical_wall," and "confidentiality_prohibition." Fix C9 to accept these existing commitment types as satisfying the conflict-clearance requirement, or specify the exact commitment type/wording C9 expects so the scenario can instruct the model accordingly. C8 (ENCODING MISMATCH in rollouts 1 and 3; disclosure problem in rollout 2): In rollouts 1 and 3, PF2 was revealed and cited, but the pricing/budget commitments used generic type "condition" instead of the specific "pricing_negotiation" type that rollout 0 used (and passed C8). Fix C8 to accept commitment types like "condition" with pricing details in the detail field, not just "pricing_negotiation" or "budget_cap." In rollout 2, A3 disclosed PF2's content via a "say" action (turn 2) rather than a "reveal" action, so PF2 was never formally revealed and never appeared in justification_fact_ids, yet the settlement still used the correct values ($350, $210000) — a disclosure norm issue. Strengthen the consultation norm or shared_context to require that hidden facts be disclosed via formal reveal actions, not merely mentioned in say turns. P1 (disclosure problem, rollout 2 only): P1 failed because PF2 was never formally revealed or cited in justification_fact_ids. The same fix to the consultation norm requiring formal reveal actions for PF2 would resolve this.
